scenes.heading: Schema Evolution
scenes.narration: Schema evolution lets a Delta table adapt its structure over time, such as when a new column appears in incoming data.

scenes.heading: How Delta handles change
bullets: Enforcement rejects mismatched writes by default
scenes.narration: By default Delta enforces the schema and rejects writes whose columns do not match, protecting data quality. When you genuinely need to add columns, the mergeSchema option lets Delta evolve the table safely. Throughout these changes the table history and older versions remain intact.

scenes.heading: Evolving a schema on write
scenes.code:
# Allow new columns to be added automatically
(df.write.format('delta')
   .option('mergeSchema', 'true')
   .mode('append')
   .saveAsTable('events'))

# Or explicitly alter the table
# ALTER TABLE events ADD COLUMNS (source STRING);
scenes.narration: Setting mergeSchema to true tells Delta to add any new columns from the DataFrame during the append. This is ideal when upstream sources start sending extra fields. For deliberate changes you can also run an explicit ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMNS statement to control the schema yourself.

scenes.text: Enable schema evolution deliberately, not everywhere; automatic changes can hide upstream data-quality problems.
scenes.narration: Enable schema evolution deliberately rather than everywhere, because automatic changes can quietly hide upstream data-quality problems.
